mechanism_narrative: Sustained recovery in WORKPLACES mobility, likely driven by easing of work-from-home mandates or business restrictions, indicates a return to normal routines, driving RETAIL_REC up over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than over the last 28 days despite WORKPLACES recovery, suggesting policy changes did not translate to retail.

mechanism_narrative: A significant week-on-week increase in TRANSIT mobility above a certain threshold signals increased public movement for various purposes, which will boost RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises by more than 5 points week-on-week
failure_condition: TRANSIT rises by more than 5 points week-on-week, but RETAIL_REC declines in the subsequent 14 days.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in RESIDENTIAL mobility indicates people are spending less time at home and more time out, leading to increased out-of-home activities including retail, thus improving RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL mobility continues to decline, but RETAIL_REC does not improve over the next 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: When WORKPLACES mobility increases while RESIDENTIAL mobility decreases concurrently, it strongly indicates a shift towards out-of-home activities and commuting, directly benefiting RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: WORKPLACES increases and RESIDENTIAL decreases, but RETAIL_REC remains flat or declines over the next 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in PARKS mobility suggests a general increase in outdoor activity and willingness to leave home, which can translate into more retail visits and a positive change in RETAIL_REC over the next week.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises by more than 10 points week-on-week
failure_condition: PARKS mobility rises by more than 10 points week-on-week, but RETAIL_REC does not increase in the following 7 days.

mechanism_narrative: The simultaneous recovery in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT mobility, combined with a decrease in RESIDENTIAL mobility, creates a strong positive feedback loop for RETAIL_REC as people are actively moving and engaging outside their homes, leading to an increase over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: Despite concurrent increases in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT and a decrease in RESIDENTIAL, RETAIL_REC does not improve over the next 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: The sustained low level of RETAIL_REC mobility, despite some other positive indicators, suggests a persistent behavioral reluctance or underlying conditions that will keep it low or further depress it in the short term over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC shows a significant increase in the next two weeks, contradicting the observed inertia.

mechanism_narrative: A continued decline in GROCERY_PHARM mobility, even for essential services, indicates a broader reduction in out-of-home movement for daily needs, which will negatively impact discretionary retail and drive RETAIL_REC down over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM falls below -5% and continues to decline
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM continues to decline, but RETAIL_REC increases over the next 28 days.
